message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to cancel a date because I'm really tired. Let me start by understanding the situation better. I've been talking to this guy for two weeks, and we had our first date a week after we started talking. That went well, and then we had our second date on Wednesday. Now it's Friday in Australia, so we're in a different time zone, but I think that's just a detail. On the second date, I mentioned something to him about some things she said over the last week that have been a bit full on, like planning too far ahead. I just wanted to be fully transparent, but I also said that it hasn't freaked me out, I just wanted to let him know I wanted to take things slow. He understood, and we made plans to hang out on Friday night to watch a movie. That would have been our third date. But here's the thing: I've had an incredibly long week. I only got about four hours of sleep and worked from 7 am to 5 pm with only a half-hour break. So by Friday, I'm absolutely shattered. He asked me around 5:30 pm if we were grabbing dinner or if he should get something himself. I told him I feel horrible but I'm absolutely exhausted and would probably just fall asleep. I asked if we could do it on Sunday instead, and I said I'd take him out to lunch, I'd pay, and we could watch a movie. Now, I'm worried that after him thinking I wanted out of the relationship, plus now canceling the date, he might think I'm not interested anymore. Is it AITA (Ask a Guy) for rescheduling a date when he already has doubts about me? Alright, so I need to figure out if it's right or wrong to cancel the date because I'm tired. Let's break this down. First, communication is key in any relationship. I told him I was exhausted and wanted to reschedule. That seems honest and considerate. But I'm also worried that he might interpret this as a lack of interest, especially if he already had doubts about me. Is it wrong to cancel a date because I'm tired? Well, everyone has off days, and it's okay to prioritize self-care. But in the context of a new relationship, where trust and interest are still being established, canceling a date could send mixed signals. On the other hand, being honest about my feelings and needs is important. It shows maturity and respect for the relationship. But I also need to consider how this action might be perceived by him, especially if he's already uncertain about the relationship. Maybe I should think about how I would feel if the situation were reversed. If he was tired and wanted to reschedule, would I think he wasn't interested? Probably not, as long as he communicated honestly. But in this case, I'm the one canceling, and he might be more sensitive because he already had doubts. So, is it AITA to reschedule in this situation? I think it's more about how I communicate the rescheduling. If I explain that I'm just tired and want to ensure I'm fully present on our next date, that could alleviate his concerns. But if I just cancel without a clear reason, he might think I'm losing interest. Also, offering to make it up by taking him out to lunch on Sunday shows initiative and a willingness to make the relationship work, which is positive. In conclusion, while it's understandable to want to reschedule due to fatigue, the way I communicate this is crucial. Being honest and reassuring him that I still want to spend time together can help prevent him from misinterpreting the cancellation as a lack of interest.
